$description: Design tokens, in the W3C Design Tokens Format Module shape (2025.10). THE authority for every design value in the product. DTCG-SHAPED, PARTIALLY NATIVE, NOT YET CONFORMANT -- and the middle word is the correction. This paragraph used to say "every primitive value is a string", which stopped being true once the structured types were admitted: `fontWeight`, `number`, `duration` and `cubicBezier` are already at their 2025.10 representation. Counted rather than estimated: 47 primitives remain in a legacy string form (28 color, 17 dimension, 2 fontFamily) against 6 already native. A conformance claim that overstates the gap is the same defect as one that understates it. WHAT THE REMAINING 47 NEED: color wants `{colorSpace, components}` where it now holds a hex string, and dimension wants `{value, unit}` where it holds a CSS length -- with the unit mandatory even at zero, which is why the bare "0" in `space` is the one entry that must change shape rather than merely gain an alternative (verified against designtokens.org/TR/2025.10 on 2 Sep 2026; evidence-register E22, E23). `$modes` IS NOT CONFORMANT EITHER, and its destination is now two-staged rather than one. The schema enumerates its properties and sets `additionalProperties: false`, so a root `$modes` fails it. `$extensions` under a vendor key is the spec's sanctioned home for proprietary data and is a correct INTERIM destination -- but calling it the final one, as an earlier revision of this paragraph did, was wrong: 2025.10 ships a Resolver module whose stated purpose is exactly multiple token contexts (theme, density, contrast), and it recommends orthogonal modifiers, which is this file's "theme owns colour, density owns geometry" rule under another name. The end state is a resolver document with theme and density as modifiers, not a proprietary block that happens to validate. packages/tokens/generated/tokens.css is DERIVED from this file and is never hand-edited (law 27). Three layers, and the middle one is the point: primitives are raw values, semantics name a ROLE, and components reference semantics. A screen that reaches past the semantic layer to a primitive has hardcoded a decision the design system is supposed to own -- the generator refuses that edge rather than trusting it not to happen.

color.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Raw material with no opinion about use, which is why there is no `color.error` here: a primitive named for a meaning has taken the semantic layer's job, and the day dark mode arrives it is the wrong colour under a name nobody can change.

scrim.$description: Black at 90% alpha, and the number is not arbitrary. A scrim dims the page, and a black page cannot get darker: at 72% the ground moves from 0A0A0C to 030303, a ratio of 1.04. What it must actually suppress is the TEXT behind it, which at 72% still reads at 2.03:1. 90% crushes that to 1.2. A light theme's 60% would do nothing here.

neutral.$description: PRIMITIVE layer, LIGHT theme. The paper-side neutrals: every value here also appears in the printed document palette, so a payslip and the screen it was approved on are the same greys.

red.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Signal red, desaturated so a deduction never looks like an alarm.

100.$description: Bone, never pure white. White on black is the harshest pair available and it vibrates.

850.$description: A HALF STEP, and it exists because the dark ladder is compressed where light is not. Between `raised` at 900 and `overlay` at 800 there was no room for a hover that reads as a lift rather than as a change of layer.

1000.$description: The well. Wells, inset rows and the frame — the only true black in the system.

ink.$description: PRIMITIVE layer, DARK theme. A separate family from `neutral` on purpose: dark is never printed, so it is not bound by paper. BLACK IS THE FLOOR — 1000 is true black and every surface lifts off it, which is the only way a recessed well can exist on a black ground. The page sits a hair above the floor rather than on it.

navy.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Executive navy, from the document palette. It is INK in light -- the colour that carries authority in a heading or a total -- and it has no dark counterpart, because on the dark ground it measures 1.40:1. There the same job is done by weight.

teal.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Governance teal, from the document palette. One ramp, both themes, different steps: light takes 600/700, dark takes 500/400. Chroma RISES on dark — and rises less far on true black than it did on a mid-dark ground, because black amplifies it.

green.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Signal green — FOREST, not emerald, and that is the load-bearing choice. At 144 degrees it sits 34 off the governance teal; an emerald would have been the teal's neighbour, and "approved" would have been a shade of "clickable". Light values are the document palette's own.

sky.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Informational blue, for a state that is neither good nor bad — `submitted` and its kin. Distinct from `navy`, which is ink rather than status. Light values are the document palette's own.

space.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. A 4px scale, so spacing is chosen from a set rather than invented per screen.

target-min.$description: WCAG 2.5.8's minimum interactive target. IN PIXELS, DELIBERATELY, and this is the one place in the file where rem is the wrong unit. It was 1.5rem, described as '24px at a 16px root' -- which is an assumption about the document rather than a property of the token, and the generator's rem-to-px conversion shares that same assumption, so the check and the token agreed with each other without either being true. A user whose root is smaller than 16px got a target below the floor while everything reported green. Typography should scale with the reader; a hard accessibility floor is a fixed promise of 24 CSS px. A primitive so that the semantic floor cannot be set smaller by accident, and a generator invariant asserts it holds in EVERY density mode, because compact is exactly where somebody would shave it.

control-min.$description: The ergonomic size of a control at comfortable density. NOT the accessibility floor -- `target-min` is that, and it is a different fact: 24px is what WCAG 2.5.8 permits, not what an enterprise control should be. Pointing a button at the floor made the legal minimum the design, which is how a system ends up with controls that are technically conformant and unpleasant to hit. In px for the same reason `target-min` is: a control that must clear a fixed pixel floor cannot be measured through an assumed root.

control-min-compact.$description: Compact density. Still comfortably above the 24px floor, which the generator asserts in every mode rather than trusting this comment.

font.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. A system stack: no web font on the critical path. The employee route has 33.6 kB of headroom under the 180 kB budget, and a font is the easiest way to spend a chunk of it for nothing.

sans.$value: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

weight.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Weight is the one typographic dimension NEITHER axis owns. `$modes.density.$axis` is `dimension`, so the generator refuses a weight override on the density axis by construction -- which is what makes weight able to carry hierarchy at BOTH densities, where size cannot: `density.compact` rebinds `semantic.type.heading` to the same step as `semantic.type.body`.

leading.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Line height as a UNITLESS multiplier, which is why it is `number` and not `dimension`. The multiplier form scales with whatever font size resolves at the time, so leading follows the density axis WITHOUT being rebound by it -- a `dimension` leading would need a compact override for every size override, and would then be a token claimed by a second axis. Named `leading` rather than `line-height` because a hyphenated top-level group breaks the group recovered from a custom property; see assertGroupNamesProjectUnambiguously.

duration.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Native DTCG 2025.10 form -- an object, not the string '1600ms'. It is admitted because the generator can SERIALIZE it, which is the rule that kept this type out until the serializer existed.

easing.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. `in-out` is the exact four-point form of the CSS `ease-in-out` keyword, so the token is the same curve the stylesheet shipped rather than an approximation of it. One curve, because one animation exists; law 31 wants a second real use case before a motion ladder.

semantic.$description: SEMANTIC layer. Names a ROLE, not a value. This is the layer the stylesheet and the component tier are allowed to use, and the reason a theme change is a token change rather than a sweep through every screen. Two independent axes rebind this layer: THEME rebinds colour, DENSITY rebinds geometry. Nothing rebinds both.

accent-active.$description: Pressed continues the direction hover started, one step further: 600 to 700 to 800 here, 500 to 400 to 300 on dark. A press that looks the same as a hover reports nothing about whether the pointer ever went down.

accent-hover.$description: Hover goes DARKER on light and BRIGHTER on dark.

overlay.$description: The light ladder runs out of headroom at white, so overlay and raised share a value and the boundary is carried by the border and the scrim. Dark has room above raised and gives the overlay a step of its own.

raised-hover.$description: SECONDARY HOVER USED TO BE `sunken`, which is the same borrowing that had an info banner wearing the accent tint: a recessed well and a hovered button are different facts, and one token cannot move for one of them without moving for the other. It resolves to the same primitive as `page` in light and to a step of its own on dark, which is exactly the freedom the role buys.

heading.$description: Navy is ink here. In dark this role resolves to near-white.

space.$description: GEOMETRY. The density axis rebinds these, which is why the stylesheet must never reach the space primitives directly -- there would be nothing in between for compact to change.

control.$description: GEOMETRY of an interactive control -- button, input, combobox trigger.

row.$description: GEOMETRY of a repeated row: a list item today, a grid row in stage 6.

container.$description: GEOMETRY of a bounded region. Separate from `surface`, which is that region's COLOUR and moves on the theme axis instead.

type.$description: GEOMETRY of text. Density may tighten these; theme never touches them.

leading.$description: Line height per text ROLE. Separate from `type`, which is the same text's SIZE and moves on the density axis; leading is a multiplier of whatever size resolves, so it needs no density override to follow one.

weight.$description: Weight per text ROLE, and the ONLY thing distinguishing a heading from body text under `density.compact`, where `type.heading` and `type.body` resolve to the same step. Before this existed the compact heading was hierarchy carried by nothing.

motion.$description: The motion language. Reduced motion stays STRUCTURAL CSS rather than a third axis: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` removes the animation entirely, and one behaviour is not a ladder. A second class of reduced-motion response -- transitions shortening rather than vanishing -- would be the evidence for an axis, and it does not exist yet.

stroke.$description: Border WIDTH. See the note on semantic.border, which owns border colour.

font.$description: Typeface ROLES. Owned by neither axis -- a theme does not change the typeface and neither does density -- but they belong here so the stylesheet has no reason to reach a primitive.

target.$description: The minimum interactive target. WCAG 2.5.8 permits 24x24 CSS px or a documented exception; Xforge takes the stricter house rule that system targets meet it in EVERY density mode. Tokens can only guarantee the values a component is built from -- a 20px icon button can still be composed from compliant tokens -- so the rendered check belongs to a later stage and this is the static half.

component.$description: COMPONENT layer. Deliberately tiny, and the restraint is the rule rather than the token type. IT WAS "GEOMETRY-ONLY", WHICH WAS THE WRONG LAW. Every component token here happens to be geometry, and that is a fact about today rather than a constraint worth freezing: it would forbid `component.data-grid.selection-surface -> semantic.surface.selected` on the grounds of TYPE, when the thing that actually matters is whether the component independently supports that customisation. THE LAW IS: a component token may specialise any semantic role, but only where independent customisation of that component is a supported operation -- and it must alias a semantic role, never a primitive. The direction is what is inviolable; the type never was.

$modes.$description: The two independent axes. Each mode names only the tokens it rebinds; everything else is inherited from the base. The generator REFUSES an override of a token that does not exist, an override whose $type does not match the axis, and any token claimed by both axes -- because with equal-specificity selectors, a token overridden on both axes would be decided by which block the generator happened to emit last, and that turns source order into architecture.

theme.$description: Owns COLOUR. Rebinds roles, never component structure: because the component tier aliases semantics and the generated CSS preserves those aliases as var() references, rebinding a role here changes every component that uses it without one component token being restated.

accent-hover.$description: Hover goes BRIGHTER on dark and darker on light.

raised-active.$description: PRESSED GOES UP HERE AND DOWN IN LIGHT. On paper there is room below white; on this ground `raised` already sits two steps off true black, so the only direction left that reads as pressure is towards the light. It stops at 800 rather than 750, which is the disabled fill -- a pressed control and a dead one must not land on the same colour.

sunken.$description: True black. Recessed is darker, as in light — and on this ground the recess IS the floor, which is why the ramp has a 1000.

default.$description: Heavier than a hairline because a floating surface needs it: against a 90% scrim the overlay separates by only 1.23:1, so on black the edge is the border rather than the tint.

density.$description: Owns GEOMETRY. `semantic.target.minimum` is deliberately NOT rebound: compact is precisely where an interactive target would get shaved below the accessible floor, and the generator asserts the floor holds in every mode.
